sections.h2: Fastest way to sell in Lower Paxton Township
sections.html:
A cash sale is the fastest route in Lower Paxton, and the main gating item is the sewer settlement form that your closing agent has to send to the township authority. Listing with an agent gives more exposure, but it adds showings, buyer financing and appraisal steps that a cash buyer skips.

Lower Paxton is the most populous municipality in Dauphin County, with an estimated 55,564 residents, about 9 miles northeast of Harrisburg. Interstates 81 and 83 both run through it. Sellers who ask for speed here are usually dealing with an inherited house, a relocation, a rental they no longer want to manage, or deferred maintenance.

  • Choose your closing date first, then work backward on payoffs and utility balances.
  • Ask your closing agent to submit the township sewer transfer form early.
  • Confirm in writing who pays the 2 percent combined transfer tax.

Owners live in about two thirds of the housing, 66.5 percent, so a third of homes are rentals or otherwise not owner-occupied. A typical owned home is valued at $284,700 and typical rent is $1,417. Those are modest numbers next to the Philadelphia suburbs, though transfer tax and closing costs still add up. A landlord selling a rental pays the same percentage, so settle the split before you sign.

Linglestown in the northeast, Paxtonia in the center and Colonial Park in the west and southwest are the main named communities, and children attend the Central Dauphin School District. Many neighborhoods date from the postwar suburban boom, so older systems are common. Use the community name in your listing.

sections.h2: Sewer and stormwater accounts at sale
sections.html:
Lower Paxton's sewer authority requires settlement agents to request balances on a specific form before a sale or refinance. The form can take up to five business days to be reviewed and returned, so start the day the contract is signed.

  • The completed Sewer and Stormwater Services Transfer Form goes to the authority's settlements email address or by fax.
  • A new sewer account carries a $15 processing fee collected at settlement.
  • The authority bills in arrears each January, April, July and October, so ask your settlement agent to prorate a mid-quarter sale. A flat residential sewer rate and a single family stormwater fee appear on the same quarterly bill.
  • Delinquent accounts can go to a collection law firm, and unpaid charges become a lien that follows the property.

If your account is on automatic withdrawal, call the Sewer and Utilities Department at 717-657-5617 so the draft stops after the sale. Bills stay in the owner's name, which matters when you own a rental and a tenant normally pays the household bills.

sections.h2: How do Lower Paxton property taxes work?
sections.html:
Real estate is taxed by the township, Dauphin County and the Central Dauphin School District, and the school district is by far the largest bill at 18.2934 mills for 2025 to 2026. Township assessments rest on a January 2002 base, adjusted for new construction and appeals, so the figure on your bill can differ a great deal from market value. Earned income tax is 2 percent, with 1.5 percent to the school district and 0.5 percent to the township, and the local services tax is $52 for people who work in the township.

Interim notice mailed March 1March 1 to April 30May 1 to June 30July 1 to December 31

Unpaid taxes pass to the Dauphin County Tax Claim Bureau after December 31. Interim bills follow new construction, pools and additions, so a seller who finished a basement or built a deck may owe an interim bill even after the regular one.

Dauphin County accepts annual appeals after June 1 and no later than 4:30 p.m. on August 1, and a late filing is rejected even if it was mailed on time. An appeal from a new or revised assessment must arrive within 40 days of the notice. The filing fee must come with the form and is not refunded, and all delinquent taxes on the parcel must be current before the Board will accept or hear it.

The Board of Assessment Appeals sits in the Administration Building at 2 South 2nd Street, Harrisburg, and takes filings by mail or in person on weekdays. The aggrieved party must appear at the hearing, and anyone representing an owner must be a Pennsylvania attorney who brings a power of attorney.

sections.h2: What closing costs should a Lower Paxton seller expect?
sections.html:
The state realty transfer tax is 1 percent, the township levies one half of one percent by ordinance, and the Central Dauphin School District levies one half of one percent. Together that is 2 percent of the sale price, collected at settlement by the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds. Both parties are jointly liable under state law, so allocate it in the contract. Exempt transfers include certain moves between close family members and property that passes by will or intestacy.

Add prorated real estate tax, sewer and trash charges, any agent commissions, and payoff of any mortgage or lien. Ask the township codes office whether any sale-related inspection or certificate applies to your address.

Start by choosing the closing date you want, then ask your closing agent to send in the sewer transfer form on the day the contract is signed. Allow up to five business days for the authority to return balances. While you wait, find out whether your tax bills are current, since an unpaid balance can reach the Tax Claim Bureau after December 31 and a delinquent parcel cannot be appealed until it is current.

Next, line up payoffs for any mortgage or lien and gather your sewer and trash account details. If your sewer account is on automatic withdrawal, call the Sewer and Utilities Department so the draft stops after settlement. At the table, check that the transfer tax shares, the prorated taxes and the new account fee all match your contract. A cash sale tends to be quick here because no lender sits in the middle, though the sewer form still sets the pace, so file it first. Cash Home Buyers CA can give you a figure to compare against a listing.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Lower Paxton Township?
faqs.a: The total is 2 percent of the sale price: 1 percent to Pennsylvania, one half percent to the township and one half percent to the Central Dauphin School District. The county Recorder of Deeds collects it at settlement.

faqs.q: Does the Lower Paxton sewer authority need anything before closing?
faqs.a: Yes. The settlement agent must send the Sewer and Stormwater Services Transfer Form and allow up to five business days for balances. The authority charges a $15 new account fee at settlement.

faqs.q: What is the Dauphin County assessment appeal deadline?
faqs.a: August 1 at 4:30 p.m., with filing allowed after June 1. A new or revised assessment can be appealed within 40 days of its notice.

faqs.q: Who collects real estate tax in Lower Paxton Township?
faqs.a: An elected tax collector handles real estate tax payments for the township, county and school district. Unpaid taxes go to the Dauphin County Tax Claim Bureau after December 31.

faqs.q: How does the sewer bill work if I sell mid-quarter?
faqs.a: The authority bills in arrears each January, April, July and October. Ask your settlement agent to prorate the quarter so you pay only for the days you owned the house.
